prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules bring a chosen protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell's own machinery removes it

statement.case_for: I have moved from B025 to B014. The first round showed that my candidate has support from me alone, and the discussion did not remove the objection that it builds on Marcus theory and on Dutton's work in natural proteins, so I cannot present it as the committee's best-supported achievement this year. B014 is the shortlisted achievement with the widest explicit support and the best mechanistic evidence base: induced proximity through a ternary complex is a physical-chemical principle with measurable cooperativity, geometry and kinetics, and it has been confirmed independently over two decades across many ligases and targets. Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated the designed bifunctional degrader. Handa identified cereblon as the target of thalidomide, which showed how a small molecule can reshape an E3 ligase surface and redirect it to new substrates. That mechanism explains drugs already approved, which answers the maturity concern I raised in round 1, because the principle is clinically validated even though no heterobifunctional degrader is approved. I choose Handa over Ciulli as the third name because the cereblon result is a discovery about mechanism that the PROTAC concept does not imply, whereas Ciulli's VHL ligands and structures, while valuable, refine a design that Crews and Deshaies had already shown to work. I do not claim this is the only defensible trio.
statement.case_against: Credit is the weak point. Three names cannot cover the 2001 PROTAC paper authors Sakamoto and Kim, Ito, Gray, or Ciulli, and the citation joins a designed-molecule lineage to a mechanism-of-an-existing-drug lineage, which a careful reader may see as two discoveries. Clinical benefit from heterobifunctional degraders is still maturing, and I have not verified approval status from the expert reports, so my statement on this point rests on recall and should be checked against them. Choosing this configuration also means I leave aside B025, which I still regard as mature and cleanly attributed, and I accept that the committee's weight on tools and modalities over a stated mechanism differs from mine.

responses.point: Zou argues that Crews, Deshaies and Handa let one citation cover both the heterobifunctional and the molecular-glue arms, that approved lenalidomide-class glues validate the principle clinically, and that B025 is a serious alternative for a later year rather than a reason to delay B014.
responses.response: You have persuaded me on the clinical point. In round 1 I treated the lack of an approved PROTAC as a reason for caution, but the glue-class drugs are approved and their mechanism is understood in structural terms, so the principle is validated even if one modality is not. I also accept your point that B025 has opened fewer experiments for chemists, and I have moved to your trio. I share your worry that the citation can look like two lineages stitched together, so I would word it around the shared principle, recruitment of a ligase to remove a protein, and not around the word PROTAC.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, ranks B014 first as induced proximity and asks exactly who discovered what and when, since the PROTAC concept and the cereblon-glue mechanism compete for three places.
responses.response: My round-1 answer was that the expert report must separate the two discoveries, and I still hold that. On the evidence in front of us, Crews and Deshaies conceived and showed the designed degrader in 2001 together with Sakamoto and Kim, and Handa with Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target in 2010. These are distinct discoveries joined by one principle, and I think they can sit in one citation if it states the principle. I would ask the chair to record that Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are left out for lack of seats and not because their work is doubted.

responses.point: Aqvist backs Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli and values the quantitative link between ternary-complex thermodynamics, cooperativity and degradation, while warning that a PROTAC-only prize leaves out the glue lineage that a careful reader will notice.
responses.response: I take your physical argument seriously, and cooperativity in the ternary complex is the kind of mechanism I value. But your own reservation about the glue lineage is the reason I prefer Handa to Ciulli. A Ciulli trio would be a PROTAC prize that leaves out the one arm with approved drugs, and a Handa trio covers both arms in one citation. If the committee prefers Ciulli, I would not oppose it as a scientific matter, and the ternary-complex structures can be cited as supporting work.

responses.point: Chabes prefers a two-part prize, B014 for Crews and Deshaies alone and B042 for Liu alone, so that two chemical reactions made programmable are recognised and the trainee-credit question in base editing is avoided.
responses.response: Giving Liu alone is the cleanest attribution of the base-editing options, and I agree with your reasoning. I still doubt that base editing adds a chemical principle beyond what the 2020 genome-editing prize covered, and two chemical-biology parts in one year would weaken the case for each. I also cannot name a third seat for the two-part version without dropping Handa, which would remove the glue arm. I keep B042 as an alternative and prefer a single, well-framed B014.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports confirm the dates and priority for the 2001 PROTAC work and the cereblon identification, and the present approval status of heterobifunctional degraders, which I am stating from recall.
Whether the committee will accept Handa over Ciulli as the third name, and whether one citation can cover the PROTAC and glue arms without reading as two discoveries.
Whether the committee gives enough weight to a stated physical mechanism such as B025 in a later year, which I am setting aside now but not abandoning.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requires recusal for B014, B025 or B042. My research on proton and electron transfer in cytochrome c oxidase is scientifically close to B025, which I disclosed in round 1, and that proximity is a further reason not to press B025 against the broader support for B014. I have no personal or institutional tie to Crews, Deshaies or Handa. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, which is not relevant to any candidate.
